title: Network Uptime Credits on VPS and Dedicated Servers
content:
**The credit.** For a calendar month whose recorded network downtime exceeds what the tier's monthly network uptime commitment allows, the customer may claim the tier's credit percentage of the monthly fee per started hour of excess downtime, up to the tier's largest credit for one month, issued as account credit. The monthly fee is the amount of the line paying the term covering that month divided by its months covered. One credit is issued per server per calendar month.

This rule covers every server in the VPS and Dedicated Servers range.

## The quantities

| Quantity | What it is |
|---|---|
| Recorded network downtime | The network downtime beyond scheduled maintenance, in minutes, on the server's usage report for that calendar month |
| Excess downtime | The recorded network downtime beyond what the commitment allows for that month |
| Started hours | The excess downtime counted in hours, any part of an hour counting as a whole hour |
| Monthly fee | The amount of the term or renewal line that paid the term covering that month, divided by the months that line covers |
| Credit | The credit percentage per started hour multiplied by the started hours, held to no more than the largest credit percentage, applied to the monthly fee and rounded half up to the cent |

The credit is issued as account credit on the customer's Harborline account. A server that already has an uptime credit for a calendar month is not credited again for that month.

## Started hours at the boundary

| Excess downtime | Started hours |
|---|---|
| 1 to 60 minutes | 1 |
| 61 to 120 minutes | 2 |
| 121 to 180 minutes | 3 |

## Hypothetical worked figures

The line amount, rates and cap below are invented inputs, not Harborline figures.

A server's term covering the month was paid by a line of 600.00 covering 12 months, so the monthly fee is 50.00. That month's recorded downtime exceeds what the commitment allows by 130 minutes, which is 3 started hours.

- At a hypothetical 4 percent per started hour with a hypothetical cap of 30 percent: 3 started hours give 12 percent, under the cap; the credit is 12 percent of 50.00, which is 6.00.
- At the same rate with a hypothetical cap of 10 percent: 12 percent is held to 10 percent; the credit is 5.00.
